sections.label: System
sections.info: Change base hardware selection, region, BIOS and Sega CD/Mega-CD save file settings.

items.label: System Hardware
items.info: Runs loaded content with a specific emulated console. 'Auto' will select the most appropriate system for the current game.

items.label: System Region
items.info: Specify which region the system is from. For consoles other than the Game Gear, 'PAL' is 50 Hz, while 'NTSC' is 60 Hz. Games may run faster or slower than normal if the incorrect region is selected.

items.label: Force VDP Mode
items.info: Overrides the VDP mode to force it to run at either NTSC 60Hz or PAL 50Hz, regardless of system region.

items.label: System Boot ROM
items.info: Use official BIOS/bootloader for emulated hardware, if present in RetroArch's system directory. Displays console-specific start-up sequence/animation, then runs loaded content.

items.label: CD System BRAM (Requires Restart)
items.info: When running Sega CD/Mega-CD content, specifies whether to share a single save file between all games from a specific region (Per-BIOS) or to create a separate save file for each game (Per-Game). Note that the Sega CD/Mega-CD has limited internal storage, sufficient only for a handful of titles. To avoid running out of space, the 'Per-Game' setting is recommended.

items.label: CD Backup Cart BRAM (Requires Restart)
items.info: When running Sega CD/Mega-CD content, specifies whether to share a single backup ram cart for all games (Per-Cart) or to create a separate backup ram cart for each game (Per-Game).

items.label: CD Backup Cart BRAM Size (Requires Restart)
items.info: Sets the backup ram cart size when running Sega CD/Mega-CD content. Useful when setting the backup ram cart to Per-Game to avoid multiple larger cart sizes.

items.label: CD add-on (MD mode) (Requires Restart)
items.info: Specify which add-on to use for CD audio playback with supported Mega Drive/Genesis games.

items.label: Cartridge Lock-On
items.info: Lock-On Technology is a Mega Drive/Genesis feature that allowed an older game to connect to the pass-through port of a special cartridge for extended or altered gameplay. This option specifies which type of special 'lock-on' cartridge to emulate. A corresponding bios file must be present in RetroArch's system directory.

sections.label: Video
sections.info: Change aspect ratio, display cropping, video filter and frame skipping settings.

items.label: Core-Provided Aspect Ratio
items.info: Choose the preferred content aspect ratio. This will only apply when RetroArch's aspect ratio is set to 'Core provided' in the Video settings.

items.label: Borders
items.info: Enable this to display the overscan regions at the top/bottom and/or left/right of the screen. These would normally be hidden by the bezel around the edge of a standard-definition television.

items.label: Hide Master System Side Borders
items.info: Cuts off 8 pixels from either the left side of the screen, or both left and right sides when running Master System games.

items.label: Game Gear Extended Screen
items.info: Forces Game Gear titles to run in SMS mode, with an increased resolution of 256x192. May show additional content, but typically displays a border of corrupt/unwanted image data.

items.label: Blargg NTSC Filter
items.info: Apply a video filter to mimic various NTSC TV signals.

items.label: LCD Ghosting Filter
items.info: Apply an image 'ghosting' filter to mimic the display characteristics of the Game Gear and Genesis Nomad LCD panels.

items.label: Interlaced Mode 2 Output
items.info: Interlaced Mode 2 allows the Mega Drive/Genesis to output a double height (high resolution) 320x448 image by drawing alternate scan lines each frame (this is used by Sonic the Hedgehog 2 and Combat Cars multiplayer modes). 'Double Field' mimics original hardware, producing a sharp image with flickering/interlacing artifacts. 'Single Field' applies a deinterlacing filter, which stabilizes the image but causes mild blurring.

items.label: Frameskip
items.info: Skip frames to avoid audio buffer under-run (crackling). Improves performance at the expense of visual smoothness. 'Auto' skips frames when advised by the frontend. 'Manual' utilizes the 'Frameskip Threshold (%)' setting.

items.label: Frameskip Threshold (%)
items.info: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Manual', specifies the audio buffer occupancy threshold (percentage) below which frames will be skipped. Higher values reduce the risk of crackling by causing frames to be dropped more frequently.

items.label: Master System FM (YM2413)
items.info: Enable emulation of the FM Sound Unit used by certain Sega Mark III/Master System games for enhanced audio output.

items.label: Master System FM (YM2413) Core
items.info: Select method used to emulate the FM Sound Unit of the Sega Mark III/Master System. 'MAME' option is fast, and runs full speed on most systems. 'Nuked' option is cycle accurate, very high quality, and has substantial CPU requirements.

items.label: Mega Drive/Genesis FM
items.info: Select method used to emulate the FM synthesizer (main sound generator) of the Mega Drive/Genesis. 'MAME' options are fast, and run full speed on most systems. 'Nuked' options are cycle accurate, very high quality, and have substantial CPU requirements. The YM2612 chip is used by the original Model 1 Mega Drive/Genesis. The YM3438 is used in later Mega Drive/Genesis revisions.

items.label: Sound Output
items.info: Select stereo or mono sound playback.

items.label: Audio Filter
items.info: Enable a low pass audio filter to better simulate the characteristic sound of a Model 1 Mega Drive/Genesis.

items.label: Low-Pass Filter %
items.info: Specify the cut-off frequency of the audio low pass filter. A higher value increases the perceived 'strength' of the filter, since a wider range of the high frequency spectrum is attenuated.

items.label: PSG Preamp Level
items.info: Set the audio preamplifier level of the emulated SN76496 4-channel Programmable Sound Generator found in the SG-1000, Sega Mark III, Master System, Game Gear and Mega Drive/Genesis.

items.label: FM Preamp Level
items.info: Set the audio preamplifier level of the emulated Mega Drive/Genesis FM sound synthesizer or Sega Mark III/Master System FM Sound Unit.

items.label: CD-DA Volume
items.info: Adjust the mixing volume of the emulated CD audio playback output.

items.label: PCM Volume
items.info: Adjust the mixing volume of the emulated Sega CD/Mega-CD RF5C164 PCM sound generator output.

items.label: EQ Low
items.info: Adjust the low range band of the internal audio equalizer.

items.label: EQ Mid
items.info: Adjust the middle range band of the internal audio equalizer.

items.label: EQ High
items.info: Adjust the high range band of the internal audio equalizer.

sections.label: Input
sections.info: Change light gun and/or mouse input settings.

items.label: Light Gun Input
items.info: Use a mouse-controlled 'Light Gun' or 'Touchscreen' input.

items.label: Show Light Gun Crosshair
items.info: Display light gun crosshairs when using the MD Menacer, MD Justifiers and MS Light Phaser input device types.

items.label: Invert Mouse Y-Axis
items.info: Inverts the Y-axis of the MD Mouse input device type.

sections.label: Emulation Hacks
sections.info: Change processor overclocking and emulation accuracy settings that affect low-level performance and compatibility.

items.label: Remove Per-Line Sprite Limit
items.info: Removes the original sprite-per-scanline hardware limit. This reduces flickering but can cause visual glitches, as some games exploit the hardware limit to generate special effects.

items.label: Enhanced per-tile vertical scroll
items.info: Allows each individual cell to be scrolled vertically, instead of 16px 2-cell, by averaging out with the vscroll value of the neighbouring cell. This hack only applies to few games that use 2-cell vertical scroll mode.

items.label: Enhanced per-tile vertical scroll limit
items.info: Only when Enhanced per-tile vertical scroll is enabled. Adjusts the limit of the vertical scroll enhancement. When the vscroll difference between neighbouring tiles is bigger than this limit, the enhancement is disabled.

items.label: CPU Speed
items.info: Overclock the emulated CPU. Can reduce slowdown, but may cause glitches.

items.label: System Lock-Ups
items.info: Emulate system lock-ups that occur on real hardware when performing illegal address access. This should only be disabled when playing certain demos and homebrew that rely on illegal behavior for correct operation.

items.label: 68K Address Error
items.info: The Mega Drive/Genesis main CPU (Motorola 68000) generates an Address Error exception (crash) when attempting to perform unaligned memory access. Enabling this will simulate this behavior. It should only be disabled when playing ROM hacks, since these are typically developed using less accurate emulators and may rely on invalid RAM access for correct operation.

items.label: CD Access Time
items.info: Simulate original CD hardware latency when initiating a read or seeking to a specific location on loaded disc. This is required by a few CD games that crash if CD data is available too soon and also fixes CD audio desync issues in some games. Disabling this can be useful with MSU-MD games as it makes CD audio tracks loops more seamless.

items.label: CD Image Cache
items.info: Load CD image to memory on startup. CHD supported only. Restart Required.

sections.label: Advanced Channel Volume Settings

items.label: Show Advanced Audio Volume Settings (Reopen menu)
items.info: Enable configuration of low-level audio channel parameters. NOTE: Quick Menu must be toggled for this setting to take effect.

items.info: Reduce the volume of the PSG Tone Channel 0.
